JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Muniyappa in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioners forthcoming in the petition that, on 26.02.2023 at about 9.30 a.m. deceased Muniyappa was standing on the edge of Bengaluru-Kolar NH-75 road at Maderahalli gate, Kolar Taluk & District, intending to cross the said highway at that time, rider of Royal Enfield Interceptor motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-HG-6096 came from Bengaluru side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, due to which he lost control over his vehicle and Rathnamma vs Satish.

2
the said motorcycle went to its wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the deceased.
Due to which, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is stated that, immediately deceased was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar, but he succumbed to the said injuries on the way to hospital.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.50,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.
4. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale, healthy and was aged about 60 years and was an agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark,
miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
5. It is further stated that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-HG-6096.
In this regard, criminal case was registered against him, in Crime No.101/2023, for the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance policy holder and the respondent No.3 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. After service of the notice, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed written statements.

7. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has contended that the deceased negligently came running in the middle of the road to cross the road and when he came in front of the vehicle, the rider immediately applied the brake, due to negligent act of the deceased the accident happened but not due to the act of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-HG-6096.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent No.1.
8.

The respondent No.2, in the written statement has stated that he was earlier owner of the motor cycle which was duly insured with the 3 rd respondent vide policy bearing No.0146924544 valid from 27.03.2019 to 26.03.2024 and the policy is in force as on the date of accident.
He has sold his vehicle to a person called S.Sathish for valuable consideration.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent No.2.
9.
The respondent No.3, in the written statement has not seriously disputed the accident, and the death of Muniyappa.
Further admitted that this respondent has issued certificate of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 and the same was in force as on the date of accident.

Further contended Rathnamma vs Satish.S on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71409624/
3 that, the death was not due to accidental injuries.

It is also defence of the respondent that, there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, on the contrary, the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased himself, who was crossing the road without following the traffic rules and regulations.
It is also contention of the respondent that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.

And stated that, neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent No.3.
10.

On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this court had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Muniyappa had died in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 26.02.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., near Maderahalli Gate, on Bengaluru- Kolar NH-75 road, Kolar Taluk & District due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Royal Enfield Interceptor motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-HG- 6096 in an actionable negligence ?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and From whom?
3) What order or award?
11. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 has examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
In the cross examination of PW1, Ex.R1 and Ex.R2 are marked through confrontation.
12. On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined himself as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R3 to Ex.R6.
The respondent No.2 and 3 have not led any rebuttal evidence.
13. Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
Perused the materials available on record.
14. At the time of argument the counsel for the petitioner has relied the decision reported in 2024 ACJ 2304 between Legal Manager, Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nagamma & Others.

sentences.text: On going through the supra decisions it appears that the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, in order to discharge the burden of proof, it is unnecessary for the profounder of that defence to adduce evidence about the matter.

Contributory negligence can be and very often is inferred from the evidence already adduced on the claimants behalf or from the perspective facts, either admitted or found established on a balance of probabilities in the case.

18. My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
19.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the bike bearing No.KA-51-HG-6096, the alleged accident had taken place.

Consequently,
Muniyappa had died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.
20. On the contrary, the respondent No.1 though not disputed the accident and the death of Muniyappa, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle.
In such a situation, it is necessary to go through the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion with respect to the above point.
On going through the above point, burden is on the petitioners to prove the same on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
21. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P8
. Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.101/2023 of Kolar Rural Police Station.
Ex.P2- true copy of the first information statement given by one Nagendra,
Ex.P3-true copy of Spot mahazar, Ex.P4- true copy of Spot sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P6- true copy of Inquest report, Ex.P7-true copy of PM report and Ex.P.8-true copy of Charge sheet.

22. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Nagendra, the S.H.O. of Kolar Rural Police has registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
23.
Per contra, respondent No.1 in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner has examined himself as RW1.

He has deposed that the deceased negligently came running in the middle of the road to cross the road,, when he came infront of the vehicle the driver immediately applied the break but, due to the negligent act of the deceased this accident was happened.

He has placed e-mail copy,
65B certificate, D.L. and Pen drive as per Ex.R3 to Ex.R6.

To prove the said fact, the respondent No.1 has not examined either the rider of the offending or any independent eye witness to prove that as on the date of the accident rider of the offending vehicle had no fault in causing the accident.

24. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.1 & 3 about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.
25. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Royal Enfield Interceptor bearing No.KA-51-HG-6096 and in the said accident, Muniyappa succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2;
26.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P9 to Ex.P14 Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased and election I.D. card of petitioner No.1 & the deceased, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
27. In the case on hand, no doubt that the petitioner No.2 to 4 are major daughter and sons of Muniyappa filed this claim petition.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioner during his lifetime.
In the cross- examination PW1 has stated that petitioner No.2 to 4 are all married.
Here, it is necessary discuss the point that, father place an important role in the family.
All the children, one or the other way defendants to their parents whether they are minors or majors, married or unmarried.
But the percentage of disability may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of disability is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

Rathnamma vs Satish.S on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71409624/
6 28

In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major sons, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their father during his lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.

In this regard, relied the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court (DB), in National Insurance Company Lilmited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency,
the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application,
irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
29.
The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P12 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 15.9.1945.
The accident occurred on 26.2.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 78 years.

For his age, multiplier '5' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
30.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing agriculture and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
31.
Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

"
32. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and Rathnamma vs Satish.S on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71409624/
7 living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
33. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are four persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
34. In the present case, deceased was aged about 78 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "5" is applicable.

Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/-
per month. And Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,44,000/-
(Rs.1,92,000-Rs.48,000).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "5" which comes to Rs.7,20,000/-.
35.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

36. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 4 under the head loss of consortium.
37.

LIABILITY:
39.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Royal Enfield Interceptor bearing registration No.KA-51-HG-6096, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
40. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 27.3.2019 to 26.3.2024.
The alleged accident had taken place on 26.2.2023.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.3 being the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.

Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
41.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,29,000/- (Rupees nine lakh twenty nine thousand only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from Rathnamma vs Satish.S on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71409624/
